published_source: Printed Table D.1, column (1) (log(Sales)) of the published article (papers/mnsc/mnsc.2021.02026.pdf; the article's Appendix D, which the main text cites on p. 7355 for the Figure 4 estimates), read Nov 4 2026; the 16 printed bins and SEs equal the authors' full-data code output (the shipped log, kept in authors_code_event_coefs and authors_code_event_se) to the printed decimals; published_coef is the equal-weight mean of the eight printed post bins (+1..+7, >=+8) that event_structure.post_summary covers, and published_se is null (no bin covariance is printed); authors_code_coef is the same mean of the log bins; the authors' code re-run on the shipped 10 percent random seller sample gives a post-bin mean of 0.008972. Earlier: PanelMainAnalysis.R lines 111-136 (RT_Sales); full-data log logPanelMainAnalysis_Lines106_269.txt; plotted as RelTimeModel.png ('The Impact of SH Access on Sales: Before and After Ramp-Up'), figure number unverified without the article text (likely Figure 3). Per-horizon full-data coefficients in published_event_coefs.
replication_status: failed (random_subsample; same-sign-within-10-percent rule not met: the package ships a 10 percent random seller sample, so the printed full-data values are not reproducible from the shipped data; printed Table D.1, column (1) (log(Sales)) post-bin mean 0.046625 (bins +1..+7, >=+8), N 4,237,106; the authors' full-data log bins (mean 0.0464858) equal the printed bins to the printed decimals; the authors' code re-run on the shipped sample gives a post-bin mean of 0.008972, same sign, a gap of 81 percent of the printed mean; subsample post coefficients are all within 1.9 subsample SEs of the printed values except the >=+8 bin, z = -2.9; authors' pre coefficients are near zero, subsample pre coefficients are positive and noisy; verified against the article Nov 4 2026)
notes: gvar = gweek = first panel week with SHaccess = 1 (NA for the Aug 8 never-treated-in-window group), computed on the full balanced seller-week panel before any sample restriction, so cohorts stay correct in the unbalanced Price/Feedback samples (deriving the adoption week from the first observed treated row in the Price>0 sample produced 13 spurious cohorts). D = 1[week >= gweek] equals the authors' SHaccess row by row in every regression sample. Unstacked event study with relative-week dummies binned at <=-8 and >=+8; the authors omit RelTrtWeek == 0. ALIGNMENT DEVIATION: the authors' RelTrtWeek = round((WeekEndingDate - TreatmentDate)/7) makes week 0 the FIRST TREATED week (SHaccess = 1) for the May 12 and May 19 cohorts (Thursday access dates) but the LAST UNTREATED week (SHaccess = 0) for the Jun 6, Jun 13, Jun 21 and Jul 26 cohorts (Monday/Tuesday access dates), so their omitted category mixes treated and untreated weeks and their 'Post k' equals first-treated-week-relative time k for the May cohorts and k-1 for the other four. run_spec.R instead defines rel = week - first treated week for every cohort (rel 0 = first week with SHaccess = 1) with reference rel = -1 and bins at pre_min-1 = -8 and post_max+1 = +8, so the post average covers rel 0..7 and the pre average rel -7..-2; this is the paper's bin structure but not its reference period. Never-treated Aug 8 sellers are the reference group in run_spec.R (in the authors' regression they carry RelTrtWeek dummies from -22 to 0, i.e. they contribute to the pre coefficients). Subsample (10%) coefficient path and full-data path are stored in subsample_event_coefs / published_event_coefs. Bar-Gill, Brynjolfsson and Hak (2024), eBay Seller Hub (SH) randomized staggered rollout. Seller x week panel, 23 Saturday week-ending dates 2016-03-05..2016-08-06. Treatment SHaccess = 1[WeekEndingDate >= TreatmentDate], absorbing; 6 in-window access cohorts (May 12, May 19, Jun 6, Jun 13, Jun 21, Jul 26 2016 = weeks 11, 12, 15, 16, 17, 22) plus the Aug 8 group, whose access date falls after the last panel week and is therefore never treated in-window (31.3% of sellers). No always-treated units, no switch-offs. Seller FE + week FE, no controls, no weights, SE clustered by seller (authors: lfe::felm, exactDOF=T). DATA: the package ships only a 10% random seller sample (18,422 of 184,222 sellers; 423,706 seller-weeks); the full files need eBay legal approval (README). Prepared panel built by _work/mnsc.2021.02026/build_panel.R, which mirrors PanelMainAnalysis.R lines 15-66; log outcomes precomputed (logSales = log(GMV+1), etc.). published_coef/published_se are the FULL-DATA values from the package log logPanelMainAnalysis_Lines*.txt (stargazer output identical to the published table columns); the article PDF is not in the project so they are unverified against the printed tables. On the 10% sample fixest reproduces the authors' felm line exactly (coefficients identical to 8+ digits, SE identical to 4 digits); the subsample estimate differs from the full-data value by sampling error (SEs about 3.2x larger).

event_structure.source: PanelMainAnalysis.R lines 111-136: felm(log(Sales) ~ RelTrtWeek8pre + Pre7..Pre1 + Post1..Post7 + RelTrtWeek8onward | ID + WeekEndingDate | 0 | ID); RelTrtWeek = round((WeekEndingDate - TreatmentDate)/7) (build_panel.R), RelTrtWeek 0 omitted. In pipeline time (rel 0 = first week with SHaccess = 1) RelTrtWeek = rel + 1 for the Jun 6/13/21 and Jul 26 cohorts (Monday/Tuesday access dates; 11,454 of 12,650 treated sellers in the 10% sample) and RelTrtWeek = rel for the May 12/19 cohorts (Thursday dates; 1,196 sellers). The structure records the majority mapping: authors' <=-8 -> rel <= -9, -7..-1 -> -8..-2, omitted 0 -> -1, +1..+7 -> 0..6, >=+8 -> >= 7. The article (Figure 4, Table D.1 col 1) reports all 16 bins.
event_structure.verified: TWFE with these bins on event_time_authors_var relweek_m1 (= RelTrtWeek - 1) reproduces the authors' 16 coefficients on the shipped 10% sample exactly (max abs diff 4.9e-17 in coefficients and SEs, N 423,706); the full-data path (published_event_coefs) cannot be re-estimated from the package. Calendar bins (rel = t - g with adoption_var gweek_true; used by CSA cells) differ from the relweek_m1 bins only for the May 12/19 cohorts (9,568 of 98,480 treated rows), where RelTrtWeek = rel; TWFE on calendar bins would give max abs diff 0.0154 (mean 0.0055) vs the authors' coefficients.

presample_adopters_nov2: None (first access week 11 of 23). The Aug 8 group adopts after the panel (adoption_var gweek_true = 24).
table_source_nov2: Article p. 7355: the relative time model is 'reported in Appendix D (Table D.1, column (1)) and depicted in Figure 4' (data/text/mnsc/mnsc.2021.02026.txt).
adoption_var_note: Lead decision (Nov 2): adoption dates from the original treatment history. gweek_true = first week with WeekEndingDate >= TreatmentDate (same rule as gweek and SHaccess), extended past the panel: equal to gweek for the six in-window cohorts and 24 for the Aug 8, 2016 group (5,772 sellers), whose access falls after the last panel week (23). Within the sample D = SHaccess = 0 for that group (checked), so DiD-averaging treats it as never treated; its post-sample date is used only for event-time coding (TWFE leads, BJS lead regression), as in the authors' regression. Built by ~/did_packages/_work/mnsc.2021.02026/adopt_dates.R; gvar gweek (NA for the group) is kept.
event_time_authors_note: Lead decision (Nov 2): relweek_m1 = RelTrtWeek - 1, the authors' event week (round((WeekEndingDate - TreatmentDate)/7), PanelMainAnalysis.R lines 111-136) shifted so that their omitted week 0 is -1; defined for every seller (all have an access date, the Aug 8 group relative to Aug 8; no NA). TWFE indicators and the imputation estimator's bins use event_structure on relweek_m1; DiD-averaging (CSA) uses calendar rel = t - g (g from adoption_var gweek_true) with the same boundaries, which differs only for the May 12/19 cohorts (one week).
